summary: Self-improving agent system that iteratively modifies its own code and validates each change empirically against benchmarks, published at ICLR 2026. Uses population-based evolution over an archive of generated agents.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses the no-plan-repair gap; empirical validation pattern maps to execution-trace-driven repair in AIBlocked recovery

summary: Multi-graph memory architecture representing memory across semantic, temporal, causal, and entity graphs with policy-guided retrieval. Achieved highest LoCoMo cross-session benchmark score (0.70) in early 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses no-agent-memory-across-runs gap; episodic+semantic memory injection at Planning stage maps cleanly to existing promptRenderer and PostgreSQL stack

summary: Systematic study of LLM agent budget-awareness, finding frontier agents waste 44% of tokens on failing trajectories due to over-optimism. Introduces progressive interval estimation and early-stop training via SFT+RL, saving 28-64% tokens.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses no-test-time-compute-scaling gap; budget gate at policyEngine stage transitions prevents costly AIBlocked timeouts

summary: Mines recurring tool-call patterns from execution traces and speculatively pre-executes predicted next tools in parallel with LLM generation. 48.5% reduction in task completion time, 1.8x throughput improvement (SJTU + Microsoft Research, March 2026).
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — addresses no-speculative-execution gap but requires parallel subprocess management; feasibility lower given single-agent-per-stage constraint. Strong candidate for a future issue once parallel execution infrastructure exists.

source: AgentFactory: Self-Evolving via Executable Subagent Accumulation
summary: Self-evolving framework that preserves successful task solutions as executable Python subagent code rather than textual reflections, enabling reliable re-execution and continuous capability accumulation (Peking University / BAAI, ACL 2026).
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — related to the agent memory gap but focuses on code-as-memory rather than prompt-injection; would require a subagent library runtime not present in AgentForge. Interesting for a future refactor.

source: SelfBudgeter: Adaptive Token Allocation for LLM Reasoning
summary: Dual-phase training paradigm where the model first estimates the token budget required for a task before reasoning, then plans autonomously based on predicted difficulty. Achieves more efficient token use on variable-complexity tasks.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — overlaps significantly with BAGEN (selected); SelfBudgeter requires model fine-tuning which is out of scope for AgentForge's CLI-subprocess approach. BAGEN's heuristic scoring is more immediately applicable.

summary: Open-source ML experimentation agent (released March 2026, 21k+ stars) that runs training loops autonomously, keeps only changes that beat the current best, and uses a minimal three-file architecture. Karpathy joined Anthropic pre-training team in May 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low-Medium — AutoResearch is focused on ML experiment loops rather than software engineering orchestration. The minimal-architecture philosophy is inspirational but not directly actionable for AgentForge's feature set.

summary: Open-source framework for building, evaluating, and evolving LLM-based agents through iterative feedback loops. Agents are assessed and optimized automatically.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — broad framework focused on agent topology evolution; AgentForge's fixed CLI-subprocess model with static stage mapping makes EvoAgentX patterns hard to adopt without architectural changes.

source: From Coarse to Fine: Self-Adaptive Hierarchical Planning for LLM Agents
summary: Addresses single-level planning granularity in LLM agents by proposing adaptive hierarchical planning that adjusts detail level based on task complexity — expanding only where needed.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — maps to the plan revision gap; interesting for dynamic plan granularity in Claude's planning prompt. Still early; no open-source reference implementation found.

summary: Resource-constrained variant of PASTE using beam search over pattern candidates to balance speculative execution benefit against memory/compute overhead.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low-Medium — follow-up to PASTE (also considered_not_selected this run); same feasibility concerns apply. Worth revisiting alongside PASTE when parallel subprocess execution is unblocked.
